findings.problem: ShardWorkflow uses pub status: String and pub is_validated: bool / is_sent: bool as separate fields, allowing illegal states such as status="pending" with is_sent=true, or status="sent" with is_validated=false. The type system cannot enforce the shard lifecycle invariant.
findings.failure_mode: Downstream code can observe a shard that is marked sent but never validated, or sent with an arbitrary status string. Data corruption or silent misrouting of unvalidated shards.
findings.fix: Replace status, is_validated, and is_sent with a single enum typestate: enum ShardState { New, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }. Remove all three fields. Make the struct private and expose through fallible constructors.

findings.problem: mark_sent accepts any ShardWorkflow and unconditionally sets status to "sent" and is_sent to true, with no check that the shard was validated first. Any caller can bypass validation.
findings.failure_mode: An unvalidated shard can be marked as sent, causing downstream consumers to process data that was never validated. The function has no precondition enforcement.
findings.fix: Replace mark_sent with an enum method on a typestate-gated type, e.g. impl ShardState::Validated { pub fn validate_and_mark_sent(self) -> ShardState::Sent { ... } }. The compiler enforces that only Validated shards can transition to Sent.

findings.problem: status is a raw String field accepting any value. There is no validation, no domain enum, and no compile-time guarantee that status reflects a valid lifecycle phase.
findings.failure_mode: Typos, invalid strings, or tampered data silently corrupt shard state. Pattern matches on status cannot be exhaustive. Future developers cannot rely on the compiler to restrict valid values.
findings.fix: Replace pub status: String with a domain enum: pub status: ShardPhase where ShardPhase = { New, Validated, Sent }. Remove the separate is_sent flag and merge its semantics into the enum.

findings.problem: is_validated and is_sent are separate bools that together encode a state machine. Their combinatorial space (4 combinations) includes impossible states, and the code has no invariant enforcement.
findings.failure_mode: A shard can simultaneously be validated=false and sent=true, or validated=true and sent=true with status="new". No single function can reason about the full lifecycle without checking all three fields.
findings.fix: Collapse into a single enum: enum ShardState { New, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> } }. This makes all invalid states unrepresentable at the type level.

findings.problem: All fields of ShardWorkflow are pub, allowing external code to mutate status, is_validated, is_sent, and sent_at_epoch_ms directly without any validation or domain logic.
findings.failure_mode: Direct field mutation bypasses all invariants. External code can set status to any string, flip is_sent without calling mark_sent, or leave sent_at_epoch_ms as None after marking sent.
findings.fix: Make all fields private (or remove them entirely in favor of an enum typestate). Provide constructors and lifecycle methods on the type that enforce invariants.

findings.problem: mark_sent is a free function that mutates a struct in place and returns it, rather than a pure calculation that transforms a typed input into a typed output. The struct is I/O-adjacent (has epoch timestamp), but the function has no I/O boundary separation.
findings.failure_mode: The function cannot be unit-tested in isolation from side effects because it mutates and returns the same struct shape. Adding persistence or notification logic later will conflate core logic with shell behavior.
findings.fix: Define mark_sent as a pure function operating on a domain value: pub fn mark_sent(state: ShardState) -> ShardState. Keep I/O (persistence, notifications) in a separate shell function that calls this pure function.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms is Option<u64>. If this value is computed from epoch timestamps (e.g., nanoseconds since epoch), converting from other time units to u64 without checked arithmetic risks overflow on 32-bit targets or future-proofing gaps.
findings.failure_mode: If timestamps are derived from i64 or nanosecond-scale counters, unchecked as-casts or additions can overflow, producing incorrect timestamps that silently corrupt audit trails.
findings.fix: When computing sent_at_epoch_ms, use chrono::Utc::now().timestamp_millis() or checked arithmetic. Document the time unit assumption and consider using a typed newtime::EpochMs(u64) value object.

residual_risk: Static review only - no commands were run. The structural issues (typestate, boolean blindness, exposed fields) are architectural blockers that require code repair, not just review. Without a typestate enum, the compiler cannot prevent illegal shard states. The mark_sent free function remains a precondition-bypass vector.
